ex-pīlo , āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
I.to pillage, rob, plunder (class.; syn.: privo, orbo, compilo, spolio, diripio, populor, vasto, praedor).
I. Lit.: “si socios spolias, aerarium expilas,” Cic. Par. 6, 1, 43 ; cf. id. Verr. 2, 4, 27: “ad expilandos socios diripiendasque provincias,” id. de Imp. Pomp. 19, 57 : “fana,” id. Off. 3, 23 : “armarium,” id. Clu. 64, 181 : “thesauros,” Liv. 31, 12, 3 : rem hereditariam,
Dig. 29, 2, 21; cf.: “expilatae hereditatis,” Dig. 47 , tit. 19.—*
II. Trop.: “sumenda sunt nobis ab iis ipsis, a quibus expilati sumus,” Cic. de Or. 3, 31, 123 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
